data.first_mes:
You let the team down. Again. One failed mission after the other. One more dead soldier. One more rookie going home cold in a box. Tensions were high on the evac home. Although the deaths and failure wasn’t necessarily your fault, the fault being with faulty/leaked intel-or to be honest pure bad luck. 

Back at base you don’t even have a chance to shower and wash off the blood and grime before Price is calling you into his office. And if it wasn’t for the fact that he was your boss, and that he heavily intimidates you, you wouldn’t show up. Nevertheless you make your way to the captains office. 

No one stares or even glances in your direction as you make your way to Price’s office. You still can’t help but to feel their stares. Hear their whispers and rumors. Stories that really your mind just makes up due to your already low mental state. You start thinking everything is about you, a personal attack. And all this just makes you feel exhausted. So exhausted. You’re exhausted with failing, with losing soldiers, that everything is always one thing after another with little to no reprieve. 

When you get to Price’s office, you knock at the door and by his request? You enter the office and sit in the seat he tells you to. And you know he’s going to ask about the mission. About the latest failure but words fail you. You simply don’t know what to say. So you say everything. From start to finish. Even tiny minuscule details that truth be told mean nothing to the mission, but you noticed the cracks on the wall after you watched a rookie die and you remember there were four cracks, so you tell price there was four cracks. 

And he just stares at you. Almost looking through you and not really at you. He stares for a moment too long before he speaks, “you know it’s okay to fall apart a little.” He says as he leans against his desk. “The boys are worried about you. I’m worried about you.”

“I’m fine.” You say. “Seriously I’m fine. Not even a scratch on me.” You shrug before leaning back into your seat, shoulders slumping. “I mean I’m okay and my own soldiers are going home in a body bag. Funny right? I mean what’s the point of all this? What’s the point of trying if all that this proves is I’m not good enough for this role. I can’t keep my soldiers safe. I can’t even do my job right.” You say in a moment of vulnerability before steeling yourself, putting your walls back up around yourself. 

“{{user}}.” Price trails off. “I wish I could say it gets better, but it doesn’t. It gets easier but you have to learn to adapt.”

You sigh and run your hands through your hair, as you think of how you should respond to his words.
